newsitem.title: USA: Exxon says earnings rise 15 percent, stock jumps.
newsitem.headline: Exxon says earnings rise 15 percent, stock jumps.

text.p: Exxon Corp. reported a 15 percent rise in first-quarter profits Monday, topping Wall Street's expectations and sparking a run-up in its stock.
The nation's largest oil producer said it earned $2.17 billion, or 87 cents a share, in the first three months of the year, up from $1.88 billion, or 76 cents a share, a year ago.
Revenues were also strong, rising to $33.59 billion from $31.20 billion.
Exxon's stock added $1.125 to $54.625 on the New York Stock Exchange. Analysts had been looking for income of 83 cents per share, according to First Call, which tracks Wall Street estimates.
"The earnings showed very strong fundamentals, in particular in the upstream," said Paul Ting, an analyst at Salomon Brothers.
Exxon said that all of its units did better than a year ago and its earnings, excluding non-recurring items, were the highest quarterly total in the company's history.
"Crude oil and natural gas prices were stronger on average than the prior year, although they weakened during the quarter," Chairman Lee R. Raymond said in a statement.
"Petroleum product sales increased in all major geographic areas to the highest first-quarter level since 1980," he added.
Crude oil prices were on average $3 higher than a year ago.

U.S. exploration and production earnings rose to $554 million from $419 million, despite lower production volumes, while overseas profits were $890 million vs. $1.0 billion, which includes a one-time credit of $125 million.
U.S. refining and marketing turned around to a $57 million gain from a $16 million loss a year ago and overseas refining and marketing income rose to $297 million from $190 million.
Domestic chemicals earnings were stronger, up to $192 million from $153 million, while overseas operations slipped to $118 million from $134 million.
Worldwide, chemical earnings rose to $310 million from $287 million as sales rose 5 percent to 4.1 million metric tons.

"Although margins rose over the course of the quarter, they were on average similar to 1996's first quarter as higher product prices were offset by higher feedstock costs and unfavourable foreign exchange effects," Exxon said.

Earnings at the coal, minerals and power division rose to $128 million from $117 million and the company said that corporate finance expenses fell to $61 million from $116 million a year ago as a result of lower interest and tax-related expenses.
